sources.title: NIDDK · Eating, Diet & Nutrition for Celiac Disease

messages.title: Tell a friend
messages.message: Hey! I have celiac disease. When I eat gluten (a protein in wheat, barley, and rye), my immune system reacts and damages my small intestine. Eating gluten-free is how I take care of it. I still want to hang out and do things together — I just need to check the food first. Thanks for having my back!

messages.title: Going to someone’s house
messages.description: Reply to “How can we accommodate you?”
messages.message:
Thanks for asking! I have celiac disease and need gluten-free food, including care with how it’s prepared. Could we plan the food together before I come over?

• Please send me photos of ingredient labels, including sauces and seasonings.
• Wash hands, surfaces, dishes, and utensils before preparing my food, and keep it away from bread crumbs and gluten-containing food.
• Use fresh pasta water and avoid a shared bread toaster or oil used for breaded food.
• Please use separate spreads without bread crumbs and a clean serving utensil for my food.

I can help choose something or bring my own meal. I’m really looking forward to seeing you!

messages.title: Call a restaurant
messages.description: Feeling nervous? Follow this phone script, one question at a time.
messages.message:
BEFORE YOU CALL
Pick a dish you’re interested in and keep something nearby to jot down answers. You can read these lines out loud, pause, or ask someone you trust to sit with you.

START HERE
You: “Hi! I’m planning to eat at your restaurant and I have celiac disease. Could I speak with a manager or someone who knows how the food is prepared?”

If it’s a busy time:
You: “When would be a better time to call with a few questions?”

ASK ABOUT OPTIONS
You: “Which meals could be made gluten-free for someone with celiac disease? I’m interested in [dish]. Could you check its ingredients, including sauces and seasonings?”

ASK ABOUT PREPARATION
You: “How would you keep gluten from other food from getting into my meal during preparation and serving?”

Choose the follow-up that fits your meal:
• “Would you use clean utensils and a clean preparation area?”
• “Is the fryer also used for breaded foods?”
• “Would gluten-free pasta be cooked in fresh water and drained separately from regular pasta?”
• “Does the grill or toaster also touch regular bread or other gluten-containing foods?”

IF THEY SAY “IT’S GLUTEN-FREE”
You: “Thank you! Could you also explain how it’s prepared? I need to check both the ingredients and cross-contact.”

IF THEY AREN’T SURE
You: “Could you check with the chef? It’s okay to tell me if you can’t accommodate this.”

IF YOU NEED A MOMENT
You: “Could you repeat that a little more slowly? I’m writing it down.”

WRAP UP
You: “Thanks for checking. Who should I speak with when I arrive so I can confirm the plan before ordering?”

OR, IF IT WON’T WORK
You: “Thanks for being honest. I’ll make another food plan.”

You don’t have to decide during the call. These questions help you gather information; they don’t guarantee a meal is gluten-free. Confirm again with staff when you arrive.

messages.title: Explain why crumbs matter
messages.description: When someone offers to pick the bread off.
messages.message: Thanks for trying to help! Picking off bread or croutons doesn’t remove the gluten that may already be on the food. That transfer is called cross-contact. Could I have a fresh portion made with clean utensils, away from gluten-containing food? If that’s tricky, I can bring something else.

messages.title: Suggest an easy food plan
messages.description: Give a host a starting point.
messages.message: We could keep it simple with plain rice or potatoes, vegetables, and an unseasoned protein. Those can start out gluten-free, but sauces, seasonings, and preparation still matter. Could we check the ingredients together and use clean cookware and utensils? I can send a few foods that work for me.

messages.title: Make plans with the group
messages.message: I’m in! Can we choose the food or place ahead of time so I can check what works for my celiac needs? Send me the menu or plan and I’ll take a look. If food is complicated, I’m happy to bring my own and still hang out.

messages.title: Say “no thanks” with confidence
messages.description: You don’t have to explain everything.
messages.message: Thanks for thinking of me! I’m not comfortable eating this because I can’t confirm it works for my celiac needs. I’ll pass on the food, but I’d still love to stay and spend time with you.
